scope: Private transactional retained recursive graph handoff between local runtime invocations; source-level workers remain rejected

implementation.root_contract: Retained, fully published immutable root with checked nominal token, exact size and alignment; producer can already be settled
implementation.graph_ownership: Iterative traversal registers each unique backing in the destination, including arrays, recursive children, managed closure environments and captured backing; existing owners reused but descendants still traversed
implementation.publication: References and owner records are staged outside the destination ledger; final cancellation check precedes allocation-free commit; earlier failures release all staged references without modifying existing owners
implementation.sharing: Local immutable backing pointers and bytes remain unchanged; no serialization, copying or public FFI surface
implementation.limits: 300000 visited backings, 300000 traversed edges including duplicates, and 300000 destination owners; bounded workspace uses checked allocation admission and bad_alloc handling
implementation.failure_model: One injected workspace admission attempt plus one per newly staged owner; actual container allocation exceptions also roll back, but container-growth failures are not individually injected
implementation.source_separation: No admission or continuation/backend changes; recursive spawn/await remains rejected until packet/scheduler/result integration is qualified

coverage: Nested recursive node, function-array storage, duplicate environments and captured String reads in the receiving invocation
Producer settled before import; onward transfer after first receiver settlement
Repeated import preserves owner count; pre-existing root-only ownership does not skip missing descendants
All eight modeled workspace/owner failure points roll back with a pre-existing unrelated owner unchanged
Empty/ordinary roots, wrong token/size/alignment, faulted/settled/expected-error destinations rejected
Sixteen trials with two receiving threads and concurrent producer retirement
100001-node graph import and final release on a 256 KiB native thread stack
Exactly 300000 edges accepted with duplicate ownership deduplication; 300001 edges fail without publication
Exactly 300000 destination owners accepted, repeated import at bound succeeds, over-budget ledger rejected unchanged
Pre-cancelled requests and eight cancellation races leave either a complete import or an unchanged empty ledger
Existing recursive runtime, generated record/collection/callable bridge, function-array execution and recursive frontend rejection checks
qualification.format: Changed C++ ranges formatted; RecursiveHandoffTests.cpp passes clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Private runtime foundation only; source-level recursive worker arguments, captures, results, continuation frames and cached repeated awaits remain unsupported
Scheduler memory reservations and environment-byte accounting are not integrated with this handoff yet
Expected-error payloads, GPU placement, distributed transport and C/C++ integration remain separate work
Callers must provide fully published immutable graphs and exclusive access to the destination; this is not validation of arbitrary foreign pointers or mutable graphs
Cancellation racing with the final commit can complete a whole transaction; partial publication is forbidden
Retained payloads are not executable in a settled invocation; receiving checked reads require registration in a live context
No full-suite, other-platform, scheduler integration or performance claim
